An original block game made for HyPocket, open source and not related to any other game. Collect blocks and build with them (or pick creative mode for unlimited blocks), and keep your worlds. Your goal: light the five dark beacons hidden in the mist. Days pass and nights get dark: light them with lamps. It runs through the same path a real game will (x86-64 translator, desktop OpenGL and the direct display). Works with touch, game controllers, keyboards and mice (click to capture the pointer). The render scale, FPS limit, dynamic resolution and camera sensitivity are in Settings.
Heavy mode: 300 wandering creatures and a longer view (and a world four times larger in the quick game)
Run emulated: the game as a PC program through the launcher\'s engine (slower; tests the engine)

Sheltered: the mist and the creatures stay outside

They come with the mist and the dark. Whether they are one with the mist, or use it at night to hide from the light, we don’t know. The only thing those still alive know is that they don’t stop once they find you. They are clever, and they will do anything to drag you away. Where to? We have no idea either.

All we know is that they don’t seem to eat human flesh. So why take survivors and drag them to wherever their lair is? Again, we don’t know. The why is a frightening mystery. They take any living thing they find and drag it through the mist.

They are hard to kill. If you see one, don’t shoot and don’t try to fight: just run. That is the last desperate thing you can do to save your life. It is how I lived long enough to write this for those who will come here.

And know this: if you are reading it, I am probably already dead.

Day 3. The mist demons came back. The priest used to say the end would come with fire, but it came with mist. I left the candle burning in the window. God will see it.

Day 5. The neighbours left down the road. I am staying. This house has been mine for forty years.

Day 6. The mist touched the window today. The candle flickered but did not go out. They stood outside, watching. They don’t come in where there is light and a closed door. Not yet.

Day 9. The candles are gone.

resources.string: Notes of R. Teixeira, tower technician

The beacon towers were built before I was born. Nobody remembered what they were for. Now I know.

The mist is not smoke and not gas. It comes out of cracks in the air, one next to each dark tower. The air is torn there, and the other side is dark. I think the ones from over there come through them.

With the tower’s crystal lit, the crack closes. Relighting a crystal takes two lamps and three panes of glass. I relit one tower and the mist drew back at once.

I’ll try the next one. If anyone finds this: light the towers.

resources.string:
THEY ARE NOT DEMONS. They are messengers.

Those who are taken are chosen. The mist is a passage, not a plague.

DO NOT LIGHT THE TOWERS. The light drives them away, and drives us away from the passage.

I will wait for the mist with open arms. Come with me.

I don’t know how many days. there is no day here.

they bring people and animals and leave them down deep, where the mist is thickest. nobody eats, nobody sleeps, nobody dies. they just stand there.

I got out of the line. if you are reading this, you got out too.

don’t run. hide. light is no use here, only walls. and listen.
You woke up somewhere with no day. Don’t run: hide behind walls, and listen.
You are back. The mist let you go.
